endpoints.description: Create a relationship between two elements with its ends set: source/target for directed kinds (Generalization, Dependency, Realization, InterfaceRealization, Include, Extend, Transition, ControlFlow, ObjectFlow, Message, flows of the other diagram families), end1/end2 for undirected ones (Association with end name, navigability, aggregation, multiplicity; Link; ERD relationship; connectors). With a diagram the edge view is created too, through StarUML's own factory and its connection rules; tail/head may then be view ids or ids of models shown on that diagram.

type.description: With a diagram: a model-and-view id (see /introspect factory.modelAndView) or a toolbox item id that presets one, e.g. 'UMLComposition', 'UMLReplyMessage', 'ERDRelationshipOneToMany'. Without: a metamodel class whose relationship kind is directed or undirected.

tail.description: Source end: a model, or a view on the diagram. Id or path.

head.description: Target end: a model, or a view on the diagram. Id or path.

diagram.description: Diagram to draw the relationship on. Id or path.

parent.description: Owner of the relationship. With a diagram it is passed to the factory as the diagram editor does (default the diagram's owner); most relationship factories file the relationship under the tail model regardless. Without a diagram the default is the tail's owner when that has a list for this type (messages, edges, transitions), else the tail model. Id or path.

field.description: Without a diagram: owner list to add to; default the list typed for the relationship, e.g. 'messages' of a UMLInteraction.

name.description: The relationship's own name, drawn as a plain label on the edge (without the visibility mark); role names go in tailName/headName.

properties.description: Initial attribute values by name, as /introspect lists them: plain values for prim/enum attributes, an id or {$ref: id} for references, arrays of those for reference lists. E.g. {messageSort: "asynchCall"} for a UMLMessage, {guard: "x > 0"} for a UMLControlFlow.

tailEnd.description: Undirected relationships only: attributes of end1, e.g. {name, navigable, aggregation, multiplicity} for a UMLAssociation.

headEnd.description: Undirected relationships only: attributes of end2.

tailName.description: Undirected relationships only: the role name of end1 (tailEnd.name).

headName.description: Undirected relationships only: the role name of end2 (headEnd.name).

x1.description: Edge start in diagram coordinates; default the tail view's centre. For a sequence message, y1/y2 place it on the lifelines.

x2.description: Edge end; default the head view's centre.

endpoints.description: Build a whole diagram in one call from a compact spec per kind (class, sequence, usecase, activity, statemachine, erd, flowchart, mindmap, requirement, c4) or from text: Mermaid (classDiagram, sequenceDiagram, flowchart, erDiagram, stateDiagram with composite state blocks, mindmap, requirementDiagram, C4Context/C4Container/C4Component; notes and classDef/style colours; a flowchart also as activity or usecase; /export_text writes this Mermaid back), PlantUML, SQL DDL or JSON Schema. One undo step; laid out by Format > Layout where the kind allows. Elements named like existing ones are shown again rather than copied (reuse). upsert updates the diagram of the same name instead of adding another, and prune removes what the spec no longer has. Answers the ids of what it made, not the model.

kind.description: Diagram kind; required with spec. With text it is read from the source; 'activity' or 'usecase' reads a Mermaid flowchart as that kind, 'erd' JSON Schema as an ERD, and any kind picks the PlantUML reader.

spec.description:
class: {packages, classes: [{name, kind: class|interface|enum|abstract, package, stereotype, attributes: ['+id: long'], operations: ['+total(): double'], literals}], relations: [{from, to, type: association|directed|aggregation|composition|generalization|realization|dependency, name, fromMultiplicity, toMultiplicity}] (an aggregation or composition's from is the whole, which gets the diamond)}. sequence: {participants, messages: [{from, to, text, kind: sync|async|reply|create|delete}], fragments: [{operator: alt|opt|loop|..., guard, operands: ['else'], operandStarts, from, to}] (message indices)}. usecase: {system, actors, useCases, relations: [{from, to, type: association|include|extend|generalization}]}. activity: {lanes, nodes: [{id, name, type: action|initial|final|flowFinal|decision|merge|fork|join|object, lane}], flows: [{from, to, guard}]}. statemachine: {states: [{id, name, type: state|initial|final|choice|fork|join, parent: composite state}], transitions: [{from, to, trigger, guard, effect}]}. erd: {entities: [{name, columns: ['id int PK', ...]}], relationships: [{from, to, fromCardinality, toCardinality: '0..1'|'1'|'0..*'|'1..*', name, identifying}]}. flowchart: {nodes: [{id, name, shape: process|decision|terminator|data|document|predefined|alternate|database|manualInput|preparation|connector|delay|display}], flows: [{from, to, label}]}. mindmap: {root: {name, children: [...]}}. requirement: {requirements: [{name, type: requirement|functional|interface|performance|physical|design, id, text, risk, verifyMethod}], elements: [{name, type, docRef}], relations: [{from, to, type: contains|copies|derives|satisfies|verifies|refines|traces}]}. c4: {elements: [{id, name, type: person|system|container|component, kind (container kind, e.g. database), technology, description, external}], relations: [{from, to, label, technology, description}]}. Every kind also takes notes: [{text, on: node(s); sequence: side: left|right|over, at: message index}] and styles: {node: {fillColor, lineColor, fontColor}}. Names may contain '\n' or '
' for line breaks; edges name nodes by name, or by id where nodes have one.

mermaid.description: Mermaid source instead of spec. The diagram is named by 'name', else front matter 'title:' or a 'title' line.

text.description: Diagram source instead of spec, in format: Mermaid, PlantUML (class, sequence, use case, activity, state, IE entity, mind map, C4-PlantUML), SQL DDL (an ERD from CREATE TABLE and foreign keys) or JSON Schema (a class diagram, or an ERD with kind erd). Constructs a StarUML diagram cannot hold are refused as UNSUPPORTED_SYNTAX.

format.description: Format of text (or mermaid); detected when omitted: @start... is PlantUML, a JSON object JSON Schema, CREATE TABLE SQL, anything else Mermaid.

parent.description: Owner of the diagram; default the project, where StarUML adds the container the kind needs (a model, interaction, activity, state machine, data model, flowchart or mind map). Id or path.

direction.description: Layout direction; default TB, or Mermaid's.

layout.description: Layout preset for Format > Layout (see /layout_diagram); default flow-<direction>, hierarchy-<direction> for class diagrams.

autoLayout.description: Default true: Format > Layout after building. Sequence diagrams, lanes and a system boundary keep the computed placement.

upsert.description: Update the diagram with this name and kind under the parent if there is one: nodes already on it (same type and name) gain missing members, changed properties and colours, missing nodes and edges are added, and nothing is removed unless prune is set.

prune.description: With upsert: delete the nodes, notes and edges on the diagram that the spec does not have, in the same undo step. An element shown on other diagrams too, or owning one the spec keeps, loses only its view here.

allowDuplicateNames.description: Default false: a classifier, package, diagram, attribute, literal, entity or column named like a sibling of its kind is refused with DUPLICATE_NAME, since paths could not tell them apart.

dryRun.description: Answer what the build would do, with plan listing its creates, updates and deletes (paths, or '$name' placeholders for what it makes) and the exact /batch ops, and change nothing. ids and the diagram carry the placeholders.

reuse.description: Default true: a class, interface, enum, package, actor, use case, entity, requirement or C4 element named like one elsewhere in the project is that element shown again (Model Explorer drag and drop), not a copy; a path ('Model/Billing/Invoice') or 'Owner::Name' picks one by its owners. false always makes new elements.

diagram.description: The diagram built or updated.

updated.description: Existing nodes given members or properties.

unchanged.description: Existing nodes and edges left as they were.

shown.description: Nodes among created that show elements which existed elsewhere in the project.

deleted.description: With prune: elements and views deleted.

warnings.description: What was built differently than written.

format.description: The format text was read as.

layout.description: engine: Format > Layout arranged it; placed: the computed placement stands.

ids.description: Model and view ids of each node, by its name (or id) in the spec.

ops.description: The /batch ops applying the plan runs, in order.

endpoints.description: Find the type, palette item, relationship or command id to use, by a fuzzy query ('composition', 'state machine', 'erd entity', 'align'). Each hit has a one-line description and a minimal example request.

query.description: Words or part of an id; case and punctuation are ignored.

categories.description: Only these categories: diagram, palette, relationship, model, enum, command.

total.description: Entries that matched, before the limit.

endpoints.description: A compact text summary of a diagram: its nodes with their members and its edges as 'tail (end) -[Type "name"]-> (end) head', where an association or ERD end shows its aggregation (shared, composite), multiplicity or cardinality and role name; cut to maxChars. Cheaper to read than the element tree.

diagram.description: Diagram. Id or path.

maxChars.description: Longest text to return; default 4000. Lines past it are counted, not shown.

endpoints.description: Check the open model against StarUML's validation rules (the rules.js of the core and of the UML, ERD and other extensions, what Model > Validate runs on the saved file) and list each problem with the element and rule id. Needs no save. Read-only.

scope.description: Only problems on this element and what it owns; default the project. Id or path.

limit.description: Most problems to list; default 200. count is always the full number.

endpoints.description: Check how a diagram reads: node views stacked at one point (L001) or overlapping (L002), outside the canvas (L003), edges running through unrelated nodes (L004), names wider than their box (L005), nodes with no edge (L006) and crowded areas (L007). Each finding names the views by id and path, with a severity, a one-line fix and an autofix request to send as is.

diagram.description: Diagram; default the current diagram. Id or path.

rules.description: Rules to run, by id (L001) or name (overlap); default all.

limit.description: Most findings to list, most severe first; default 100. count is always the full number.

_parent.description: Owner id; null for the project.

path.description: Summary only: a path any id field accepts, e.g. 'Model/Shop/Order', 'Model/Shop/Order.total', 'Model/Shop/Order#pay()', and 'model path@diagram path' for a view. Absent for the project and for views without a model.

diagram.description: Element projection. Reference attributes are {$ref: id}; owned elements are {$ref: id} or, with depth > 0, nested elements.

autofix.description: A request that fixes it: POST body to path. Null where only a person can decide.

endpoints.description: Check the model for modelling mistakes StarUML's own validation does not look for: association ends without multiplicity (U001) or navigability (U002), attributes without a type (U003), relationships missing an end (U004), abstract classes without a subclass (U005), interfaces nobody realizes (U006), sequence messages that name no operation of the receiver (U007), use cases without an actor (U008), state machines without an initial (U009) or final state (U010), ERD entities without a primary key (U011) and names off the naming convention (U012). Each finding has a rule id, the element's id and path, and a one-line fix. Read-only.

scope.description: Only this element and what it owns; default the project. Id or path.

rules.description: Per rule id or name: off, or the severity to report it with, e.g. {U002: 'off', naming: 'warning'}.

naming.description: Naming convention per kind: PascalCase, camelCase, UPPER_CASE, snake_case, lowercase, a regular expression, or false to skip. Defaults: classifier PascalCase, attribute and operation camelCase, literal UPPER_CASE, package skipped.

limit.description: Most findings to list, most severe first; default 100. count is always the full number.

endpoints.description: Compare a diagram with a spec or diagram text (as /build_diagram takes them) and list what differs: nodes and edges the spec adds, elements and views on the diagram it lacks, and nodes whose members, properties or colours it changes. This is what /build_diagram with upsert and prune would do; nothing is changed.

diagram.description: Diagram to compare. Id or path.

kind.description: Diagram kind; required with spec, else read from text.

reuse.description: As /build_diagram's reuse, default true: a new node named like an element elsewhere counts as showing that element.

_parent.description: Owner id; null for the project.

path.description: Summary only: a path any id field accepts, e.g. 'Model/Shop/Order', 'Model/Shop/Order.total', 'Model/Shop/Order#pay()', and 'model path@diagram path' for a view. Absent for the project and for views without a model.

diagram.description: Element projection. Reference attributes are {$ref: id}; owned elements are {$ref: id} or, with depth > 0, nested elements.

identical.description: The diagram already shows the spec.

nodes.description: Nodes of the spec not on the diagram.

edges.description: Edges of the spec not on the diagram, 'from -> to'.

removed.description: Elements (or, where they are shown elsewhere too, views) on the diagram that the spec lacks.

endpoints.description: Record a checkpoint of the model under a label: every element's attributes, and the place in the undo history. /diff_since lists what changed after it, /restore_snapshot goes back to it. Kept in memory, at most 20, until StarUML restarts; a label taken again is replaced.

label.description: Name to refer to it by; default snapshot-<n>.

endpoints.description: List the model elements added, changed (with the attributes that differ) and removed since a /snapshot, with their paths. Views are not compared.

limit.description: Most items per list; default 200. counts are always the full numbers.

fields.description: Attributes whose value differs.

endpoints.description: Undo back to a /snapshot in one step: every operation recorded after it is undone, and one /redo brings them all back. Refused as SNAPSHOT_STALE when the undo history no longer reaches the snapshot (it was undone past, cut by StarUML's history limit, or another project is open).

remaining.description: What still differs from the snapshot afterwards; all zero unless something changed outside the undo history.

endpoints.description: StarUML and extension versions, factory ids, the metamodel catalogue, the diagram editor's toolbox, and this endpoint manifest with JSON Schemas.

include.description: Sections to return besides the versions; default all.

types.description: Restrict the metamodel section to these type names.

inherited.description: List inherited attributes with each type; default false (own attributes and supers).

modelAndView.description: What each model-and-view id creates; ids such as UMLInputExpansionNode create another model type.

kind.description: prim/enum: value; ref/refs: reference(s) to other elements; obj/objs: owned element(s); var: a reference or a plain value; custom: an object StarUML stores as a string (Font, Points).

type.description: Integer, Real, String, Boolean or Image for prim; otherwise a metamodel type name.

transient.description: Runtime state; not saved or returned.

attributes.description: Own attributes; with inherited: true, inherited ones first.

viewType.description: View class that shows this model class on a diagram.

viewTypes.description: Diagrams only: view classes the diagram accepts.

creatable.description: Which factory registers this name: /create_element, /create_element_with_view and /create_relationship, /create_diagram.

diagramTypes.description: Diagrams the group is shown for; null for every diagram.

rubberband.description: line for edges; rect or point for nodes.

creates.description: The model-and-view id the item creates.

options.description: Presets the item adds, e.g. model-init attribute values or parasitic: true for elements placed on a host view (pass containerViewId).

command.description: A command other than factory:create-model-and-view; such items cannot be created through this API unless `creates` is itself a model-and-view id.

items.description: The diagram editor's palette entries; an id in several groups is listed once.

response.description: JSON Schema (2020-12) of `data` in a successful response.

schema.description: JSON Schema of an error response body.

endpoints.description: Own keys of `app` and the own and prototype members of its managers.
